**Robert Michael Urich** (December 19, 1946– April 16, 2002) was an American film, television, and stage actor and television producer. Over the course of his 30-year career, he starred in a record 15 television series.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes-1)

Urich began his career in television in the early 1970s. After guest stints and roles in short-lived television series, he won a co-starring role in the action/crime drama series _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(1975\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (1975 TV series)")_ in 1975. In 1978, he landed the lead role of Dan Tanna in the crime drama series _[Vega$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegas\_(1978\_TV\_series) "Vegas (1978 TV series)")_, which aired on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from 1978 to June 1981 and earned him two [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nominations. In addition to his work in television, Urich also co starred in several feature films, including _[Magnum Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum\_Force "Magnum Force")_ (1973), _[The Ice Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ice\_Pirates "The Ice Pirates")_ (1984) and _[Turk 182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk\_182 "Turk 182")_ (1985). From 1985 to 1988, he portrayed the title role in the detective television series _[Spenser: For Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:\_For\_Hire "Spenser: For Hire")_, based on [Robert B. Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_B._Parker "Robert B. Parker")'s series of mystery novels. In 1988, he began hosting the documentary series _[National Geographic Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Explorer "National Geographic Explorer")_. He won a [CableACE Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CableACE_Award "CableACE Award") for his work on the series. He was also awarded a [Golden Boot Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Boot_Awards "Golden Boot Awards") for his work in [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") television series and films.

In 1993, he won an [Emmy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy "Emmy") for narrating a nature documentary. He revealed on _[The Late Show with David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Show\_with\_David\_Letterman "The Late Show with David Letterman")_ that he never knew about his nomination and win. It was sent by [FedEx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx "FedEx") to his home.

In 1996, Urich starred in the television series _[The Lazarus Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lazarus\_Man "The Lazarus Man")_. It was canceled shortly after he announced that he had been diagnosed with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"), a rare cancer, in July that year. He sought treatment for his illness while continuing his career and also worked to raise money for cancer research. He was declared cancer free in 1998 and returned to television in the [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") series _[Love Boat: The Next Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat:\_The\_Next\_Wave "Love Boat: The Next Wave")_. In 2000, he made his Broadway debut as Billy Flynn in the musical _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(musical) "Chicago (musical)")_. His last role was in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") sitcom _[Emeril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeril\_(TV\_series) "Emeril (TV series)")_ in 2001, but in the autumn of that year his cancer returned and he died in April 2002[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes.com-2) at age 55.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Urich was born and raised in [Toronto, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto,_Ohio "Toronto, Ohio"), the son of John Paul and Cecilia Monica (née Halpate) Urich.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-3) He was of [Rusyn (Ukrainian)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusyns "Rusyns") and [Slovak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovaks "Slovaks") extraction and raised [Byzantine Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruthenian_Greek_Catholic_Church "Ruthenian Greek Catholic Church").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-people-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-5) His elder brother was actor Tom Urich (1935-2022). An excellent high school athlete, Urich attended [Florida State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_University "Florida State University") on a [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") scholarship. He played backup center during the 1965–66 football season, receiving only minimal playing time, and was a member of the [Lambda Chi Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambda_Chi_Alpha "Lambda Chi Alpha") fraternity. In 1968, he earned a bachelor's degree in Radio and Television Communications. He went on to [Michigan State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_University "Michigan State University") and earned a [master's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree") in Broadcast Research and Management. He took voice lessons at the University of Chicago music school.

Urich explained in a 1997 interview with Tom Snyder that he worked in sales in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") at [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV") for $150 a week and was fired after they discovered he was moonlighting. Urich had also worked briefly as a weatherman.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After appearing in a Chicago production of _[The Rainmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rainmaker\_(play) "The Rainmaker (play)")_ with [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds"), Urich decided to pursue acting full-time after Reynolds encouraged him to move to Los Angeles and do more acting.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-7)

### 1970s–1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1970s–1980s")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg/250px-Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg)

Urich, [Maureen Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_Reagan "Maureen Reagan"), and [Jack Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Hogan "Jack Hogan") pose for a publicity photo for the TV series _The Specialists_, 1974

Urich made his television debut in a guest starring role in _[The F.B.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_F.B.I.\_(TV\_series) "The F.B.I. (TV series)")_, in 1972. The following year, he won a lead role in _[Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob\_&\_Carol\_&\_Ted\_&\_Alice\_(TV\_series) "Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (TV series)")_. It was a television adaptation of the [1969 film of the same title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_&_Carol_&_Ted_&_Alice "Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice"). It struggled in the ratings and was canceled after six episodes. He made his film debut later that same year opposite [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") in the Dirty Harry film _[Magnum Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum\_Force "Magnum Force")_ playing a vigilante motorcycle-patrol police officer. In 1975, Urich was cast in the action/crime drama series _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(1975\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (1975 TV series)")_. According to the executive producer [Aaron Spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Spelling "Aaron Spelling"), [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds") convinced Spelling to allow Urich to read for the part. Spelling was impressed with his reading and cast him in the role of "Officer Jim Street".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-8) A [mid-season replacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-season_replacement "Mid-season replacement"), it earned high enough ratings to warrant a second season. However, it was canceled in 1976 due to its violent content.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-9)

Urich's next role was on the sitcom _[Soap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap\_(TV\_series) "Soap (TV series)")_ as Peter the Tennis Player in 1977. That same year he was cast as Paul Thurston, a handsome, ego-driven talk show host in the _[Bewitched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewitched "Bewitched")_ spin-off series _[Tabitha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabitha\_(TV\_series) "Tabitha (TV series)")_, starring [Lisa Hartman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Hartman_Black "Lisa Hartman Black"). Its ratings were initially strong, but schedule changes caused ratings to drop, and the show was canceled in 1978 after 13 episodes.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-10) Shortly after, he was cast in another Aaron Spelling produced series, called _[Vega$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegas\_(1978\_TV\_series) "Vegas (1978 TV series)")_. Urich portrayed the series' lead character, Dan Tanna, a private detective who solves various crimes in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). _Vega$_ was a hit for [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") and he received two [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nominations for his work on it. By the third season, ratings had started to decline, and with little network support, _Vega$_ was canceled at the end of the third season in June, 1981. Shortly after, Urich signed with [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer") (MGM) and focused on film roles. His first film for MGM was _[Endangered Species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered\_Species\_(1982\_film) "Endangered Species (1982 film)")_ (1982), a science fiction film directed by [Alan Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Rudolph "Alan Rudolph").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-11)

After filming _Endangered Species_, Urich returned to television and starred in _[Gavilan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavilan\_(TV\_series) "Gavilan (TV series)")_. He played the title character who was a former [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA "CIA") agent turned [oceanographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanography "Oceanography"). The series, however, was canceled after seven episodes. In 1984, he starred in two more films _[The Ice Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ice\_Pirates "The Ice Pirates")_, and [Wes Craven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Craven "Wes Craven")'s _[Invitation to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invitation\_to\_Hell\_(1984\_film) "Invitation to Hell (1984 film)")_. In 1985, Urich co-starred in the film _[Turk 182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk\_182 "Turk 182")_, although it was not a commercial success. In 1985, Urich returned to episodic television as the title character in _[Spenser: For Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:\_For\_Hire "Spenser: For Hire")_. It was a hit and aired for three seasons. He also reprised the role in several television films after it was canceled: _Spenser: Ceremony_ (1993), _Spenser: Pale Kings and Princes_ (1994), _Spenser: The Judas Goat_ (1994), and _Spenser: A Savage Place_ (1995). In 1988, he hosted the documentary series _[National Geographic Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Explorer "National Geographic Explorer")_. He won a [CableACE Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CableACE_Award "CableACE Award") for his work on the series. In 1989, he portrayed Jake Spoon in the acclaimed television miniseries _[Lonesome Dove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonesome\_Dove\_(miniseries) "Lonesome Dove (miniseries)")_, a role for which he received many positive reviews.

### 1990s–2000s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1990s–2000s")]

In the 1990s, Urich mainly appeared in television films and several short-lived television series. From 1990 to 1991, he starred in the sitcom _[American Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Dreamer\_(TV\_series) "American Dreamer (TV series)")_ and the TV movie _83 Hours 'Til Dawn_. The following year, he starred in _[Crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossroads\_(1992\_TV\_series) "Crossroads (1992 TV series)")_, a drama series that aired on ABC for ten episodes. In 1993, he and [Faye Dunaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faye_Dunaway "Faye Dunaway") starred in the sitcom _[It Had to Be You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Had\_to\_Be\_You\_(TV\_series) "It Had to Be You (TV series)")_. It was critically panned and canceled after four episodes. In 1995, he narrated an extremely rare one-night showing of a Disney television documentary called _Alien Encounters: From New Tomorrowland_. It has never been shown again. In 1996, he starred in the [TNT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNT_(U.S._TV_network) "TNT (U.S. TV network)") western series _[The Lazarus Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lazarus\_Man "The Lazarus Man")_. It earned strong enough ratings to be picked up for a second season but shortly after it was renewed, he announced he had been diagnosed with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"). Its production company, [Castle Rock Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Rock_Entertainment "Castle Rock Entertainment"), opted to cancel it due to that.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-12) In 1999, he commented on their choice to do so, "There's really a law against what they did. They found out I had cancer, and they just canceled the show. They didn't ask the doctors if I could work. They didn't ask if I could go back to work."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-pittsburgh-13) In 2000, he sued them for [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-14) The lawsuit was later settled with both parties agreeing not to publicly disclose the terms.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) While undergoing cancer treatments, Urich hosted the medical documentary series _Vital Signs_ in 1997 and the [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") series _Boatworks_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-16) After a year of treatment, he was declared cancer-free and returned to television in 1998 as Captain Jim Kennedy III in _[Love Boat: The Next Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat:\_The\_Next\_Wave "Love Boat: The Next Wave")_. It aired on [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") for two seasons. In 2000, he made his Broadway debut as Billy Flynn in the musical _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(musical) "Chicago (musical)")_ and also starred in the North American tour of the musical, in 1999 and in 2000.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-20) The next year, he costarred in _Emeril_, a sitcom starring celebrity chef [Emeril Lagasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeril_Lagasse "Emeril Lagasse"). While it was critically panned, he received good notices for his work on it. It would be his last role in a television series. Urich's final television film, _Night of the Wolf_, aired on [Animal Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Planet "Animal Planet") the night before his death.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15)

## Personal life

### Marriages and children

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Marriages and children")]

Urich's first marriage was to actress Barbara Rucker in 1968. They divorced in 1974. He married actress [Heather Menzies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heather_Menzies "Heather Menzies") (1949–2017) in 1975. They adopted three children. They remained married until his death in 2002.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-people-4)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-21)

## Illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Illness and death")]

In July 1996, Urich announced his diagnosis with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"), a rare cancer affecting [soft tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_tissue "Soft tissue"). Despite his illness, he continued working, underwent treatment and advocated for cancer cure research. He received an award from the [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne") Cancer Institute and the [Gilda Radner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilda_Radner "Gilda Radner") Courage Award for his cancer awareness efforts.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-pittsburgh-13) He and his wife established the Urich Fund at the University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center to support cancer research. Additionally, Urich donated $125,000, his winnings from an episode of _[Who Wants to Be a Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Wants\_to\_Be\_a\_Millionaire\_(U.S.\_game\_show) "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire (U.S. game show)")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) He was declared cancer-free in 1998 and became the national spokesperson for the [American Cancer Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Cancer_Society "American Cancer Society") that year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6)

In November 2001, Urich shared in an interview that doctors had found [lumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor "Tumor") in his body, but a new medication had successfully treated them.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) A week before his death, he was hospitalized at [Los Robles Hospital & Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Robles_Hospital_&_Medical_Center "Los Robles Hospital & Medical Center") in [Thousand Oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousand_Oaks,_California "Thousand Oaks, California") with respiratory problems. He died there on April 16, 2002.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-23) His funeral Mass was held on April 19 at [St. Charles Borromeo Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Borromeo_Church_(North_Hollywood) "St. Charles Borromeo Church (North Hollywood)") in [North Hollywood, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "North Hollywood, Los Angeles").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6) A statement was released by his publicist Cindy Guagenti, and said Urich's wife and three children were with him when he died.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes.com-2)

Urich's body was cremated, and his ashes interred at the family's vacation home in [Prince Edward County, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_County,_Ontario "Prince Edward County, Ontario"), Canada. A memorial stands in the West Lake Church of Christ Cemetery, near their vacation home.

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Urich and his wife helped to raise money for the Eccles Performing Arts Centers at the [Park City High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City_High_School "Park City High School") in [Park City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City,_Utah "Park City, Utah"). After his death, the school established the Robert Urich Scholarship fund in his honor.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-24) In addition, they established the Robert and Heather Urich Fund for Sarcoma Research at the University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center. She also had cancer and was an [ovarian cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cancer "Ovarian cancer") survivor. Heather continued to work for the center, until she died from brain cancer on December 24, 2017, surrounded by their three children.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-25)

Urich's hometown of [Toronto, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto,_Ohio "Toronto, Ohio"), named the Robert Urich Interchange in his honor. It connects the town to [Ohio State Route 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Route_7 "Ohio State Route 7"). For his contribution to the television industry, Urich has a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") located at 7083 Hollywood Boulevard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes-1) Until [Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_(musician) "Usher (musician)") was added, he was the only person with a name starting with the letter U on the walk.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-28)

**Robert Michael Urich** (December 19, 1946– April 16, 2002) was an American film, television, and stage actor and television producer. Over the course of his 30-year career, he starred in a record 15 television series.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes-1)

Urich began his career in television in the early 1970s. After guest stints and roles in short-lived television series, he won a co-starring role in the action/crime drama series _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(1975\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (1975 TV series)")_ in 1975. In 1978, he landed the lead role of Dan Tanna in the crime drama series _[Vega$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegas\_(1978\_TV\_series) "Vegas (1978 TV series)")_, which aired on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from 1978 to June 1981 and earned him two [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nominations. In addition to his work in television, Urich also co starred in several feature films, including _[Magnum Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum\_Force "Magnum Force")_ (1973), _[The Ice Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ice\_Pirates "The Ice Pirates")_ (1984) and _[Turk 182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk\_182 "Turk 182")_ (1985). From 1985 to 1988, he portrayed the title role in the detective television series _[Spenser: For Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:\_For\_Hire "Spenser: For Hire")_, based on [Robert B. Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_B._Parker "Robert B. Parker")'s series of mystery novels. In 1988, he began hosting the documentary series _[National Geographic Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Explorer "National Geographic Explorer")_. He won a [CableACE Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CableACE_Award "CableACE Award") for his work on the series. He was also awarded a [Golden Boot Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Boot_Awards "Golden Boot Awards") for his work in [Western](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)") television series and films.

In 1993, he won an [Emmy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy "Emmy") for narrating a nature documentary. He revealed on _[The Late Show with David Letterman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Late\_Show\_with\_David\_Letterman "The Late Show with David Letterman")_ that he never knew about his nomination and win. It was sent by [FedEx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FedEx "FedEx") to his home.

In 1996, Urich starred in the television series _[The Lazarus Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lazarus\_Man "The Lazarus Man")_. It was canceled shortly after he announced that he had been diagnosed with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"), a rare cancer, in July that year. He sought treatment for his illness while continuing his career and also worked to raise money for cancer research. He was declared cancer free in 1998 and returned to television in the [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") series _[Love Boat: The Next Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat:\_The\_Next\_Wave "Love Boat: The Next Wave")_. In 2000, he made his Broadway debut as Billy Flynn in the musical _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(musical) "Chicago (musical)")_. His last role was in the [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC") sitcom _[Emeril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeril\_(TV\_series) "Emeril (TV series)")_ in 2001, but in the autumn of that year his cancer returned and he died in April 2002[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes.com-2) at age 55.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Urich was born and raised in [Toronto, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto,_Ohio "Toronto, Ohio"), the son of John Paul and Cecilia Monica (née Halpate) Urich.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-3) He was of [Rusyn (Ukrainian)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rusyns "Rusyns") and [Slovak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slovaks "Slovaks") extraction and raised [Byzantine Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruthenian_Greek_Catholic_Church "Ruthenian Greek Catholic Church").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-people-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-5) His elder brother was actor Tom Urich (1935-2022). An excellent high school athlete, Urich attended [Florida State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florida_State_University "Florida State University") on a [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football") scholarship. He played backup center during the 1965–66 football season, receiving only minimal playing time, and was a member of the [Lambda Chi Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lambda_Chi_Alpha "Lambda Chi Alpha") fraternity. In 1968, he earned a bachelor's degree in Radio and Television Communications. He went on to [Michigan State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michigan_State_University "Michigan State University") and earned a [master's degree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master's_degree "Master's degree") in Broadcast Research and Management. He took voice lessons at the University of Chicago music school.

Urich explained in a 1997 interview with Tom Snyder that he worked in sales in [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") at [WGN-TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WGN-TV "WGN-TV") for $150 a week and was fired after they discovered he was moonlighting. Urich had also worked briefly as a weatherman.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After appearing in a Chicago production of _[The Rainmaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Rainmaker\_(play) "The Rainmaker (play)")_ with [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds"), Urich decided to pursue acting full-time after Reynolds encouraged him to move to Los Angeles and do more acting.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-7)

### 1970s–1980s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1970s–1980s")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg/250px-Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Urich_Maureen_Reagan_and_Jack_Hogan.jpg)

Urich, [Maureen Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maureen_Reagan "Maureen Reagan"), and [Jack Hogan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Hogan "Jack Hogan") pose for a publicity photo for the TV series _The Specialists_, 1974

Urich made his television debut in a guest starring role in _[The F.B.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_F.B.I.\_(TV\_series) "The F.B.I. (TV series)")_, in 1972. The following year, he won a lead role in _[Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob\_&\_Carol\_&\_Ted\_&\_Alice\_(TV\_series) "Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice (TV series)")_. It was a television adaptation of the [1969 film of the same title](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_&_Carol_&_Ted_&_Alice "Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice"). It struggled in the ratings and was canceled after six episodes. He made his film debut later that same year opposite [Clint Eastwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clint_Eastwood "Clint Eastwood") in the Dirty Harry film _[Magnum Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum\_Force "Magnum Force")_ playing a vigilante motorcycle-patrol police officer. In 1975, Urich was cast in the action/crime drama series _[S.W.A.T.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.W.A.T.\_(1975\_TV\_series) "S.W.A.T. (1975 TV series)")_. According to the executive producer [Aaron Spelling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aaron_Spelling "Aaron Spelling"), [Burt Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burt_Reynolds "Burt Reynolds") convinced Spelling to allow Urich to read for the part. Spelling was impressed with his reading and cast him in the role of "Officer Jim Street".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-8) A [mid-season replacement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mid-season_replacement "Mid-season replacement"), it earned high enough ratings to warrant a second season. However, it was canceled in 1976 due to its violent content.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-9)

Urich's next role was on the sitcom _[Soap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soap\_(TV\_series) "Soap (TV series)")_ as Peter the Tennis Player in 1977. That same year he was cast as Paul Thurston, a handsome, ego-driven talk show host in the _[Bewitched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewitched "Bewitched")_ spin-off series _[Tabitha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tabitha\_(TV\_series) "Tabitha (TV series)")_, starring [Lisa Hartman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_Hartman_Black "Lisa Hartman Black"). Its ratings were initially strong, but schedule changes caused ratings to drop, and the show was canceled in 1978 after 13 episodes.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-10) Shortly after, he was cast in another Aaron Spelling produced series, called _[Vega$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vegas\_(1978\_TV\_series) "Vegas (1978 TV series)")_. Urich portrayed the series' lead character, Dan Tanna, a private detective who solves various crimes in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"). _Vega$_ was a hit for [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") and he received two [Golden Globe Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award "Golden Globe Award") nominations for his work on it. By the third season, ratings had started to decline, and with little network support, _Vega$_ was canceled at the end of the third season in June, 1981. Shortly after, Urich signed with [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer") (MGM) and focused on film roles. His first film for MGM was _[Endangered Species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered\_Species\_(1982\_film) "Endangered Species (1982 film)")_ (1982), a science fiction film directed by [Alan Rudolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_Rudolph "Alan Rudolph").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-11)

After filming _Endangered Species_, Urich returned to television and starred in _[Gavilan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavilan\_(TV\_series) "Gavilan (TV series)")_. He played the title character who was a former [CIA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CIA "CIA") agent turned [oceanographer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oceanography "Oceanography"). The series, however, was canceled after seven episodes. In 1984, he starred in two more films _[The Ice Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ice\_Pirates "The Ice Pirates")_, and [Wes Craven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Craven "Wes Craven")'s _[Invitation to Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invitation\_to\_Hell\_(1984\_film) "Invitation to Hell (1984 film)")_. In 1985, Urich co-starred in the film _[Turk 182](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turk\_182 "Turk 182")_, although it was not a commercial success. In 1985, Urich returned to episodic television as the title character in _[Spenser: For Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:\_For\_Hire "Spenser: For Hire")_. It was a hit and aired for three seasons. He also reprised the role in several television films after it was canceled: _Spenser: Ceremony_ (1993), _Spenser: Pale Kings and Princes_ (1994), _Spenser: The Judas Goat_ (1994), and _Spenser: A Savage Place_ (1995). In 1988, he hosted the documentary series _[National Geographic Explorer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National\_Geographic\_Explorer "National Geographic Explorer")_. He won a [CableACE Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CableACE_Award "CableACE Award") for his work on the series. In 1989, he portrayed Jake Spoon in the acclaimed television miniseries _[Lonesome Dove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lonesome\_Dove\_(miniseries) "Lonesome Dove (miniseries)")_, a role for which he received many positive reviews.

### 1990s–2000s

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1990s–2000s")]

In the 1990s, Urich mainly appeared in television films and several short-lived television series. From 1990 to 1991, he starred in the sitcom _[American Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American\_Dreamer\_(TV\_series) "American Dreamer (TV series)")_ and the TV movie _83 Hours 'Til Dawn_. The following year, he starred in _[Crossroads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossroads\_(1992\_TV\_series) "Crossroads (1992 TV series)")_, a drama series that aired on ABC for ten episodes. In 1993, he and [Faye Dunaway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faye_Dunaway "Faye Dunaway") starred in the sitcom _[It Had to Be You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It\_Had\_to\_Be\_You\_(TV\_series) "It Had to Be You (TV series)")_. It was critically panned and canceled after four episodes. In 1995, he narrated an extremely rare one-night showing of a Disney television documentary called _Alien Encounters: From New Tomorrowland_. It has never been shown again. In 1996, he starred in the [TNT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNT_(U.S._TV_network) "TNT (U.S. TV network)") western series _[The Lazarus Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lazarus\_Man "The Lazarus Man")_. It earned strong enough ratings to be picked up for a second season but shortly after it was renewed, he announced he had been diagnosed with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"). Its production company, [Castle Rock Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Castle_Rock_Entertainment "Castle Rock Entertainment"), opted to cancel it due to that.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-12) In 1999, he commented on their choice to do so, "There's really a law against what they did. They found out I had cancer, and they just canceled the show. They didn't ask the doctors if I could work. They didn't ask if I could go back to work."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-pittsburgh-13) In 2000, he sued them for [breach of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breach_of_contract "Breach of contract").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-14) The lawsuit was later settled with both parties agreeing not to publicly disclose the terms.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) While undergoing cancer treatments, Urich hosted the medical documentary series _Vital Signs_ in 1997 and the [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PBS "PBS") series _Boatworks_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-16) After a year of treatment, he was declared cancer-free and returned to television in 1998 as Captain Jim Kennedy III in _[Love Boat: The Next Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Boat:\_The\_Next\_Wave "Love Boat: The Next Wave")_. It aired on [UPN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UPN "UPN") for two seasons. In 2000, he made his Broadway debut as Billy Flynn in the musical _[Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago\_(musical) "Chicago (musical)")_ and also starred in the North American tour of the musical, in 1999 and in 2000.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-20) The next year, he costarred in _Emeril_, a sitcom starring celebrity chef [Emeril Lagasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeril_Lagasse "Emeril Lagasse"). While it was critically panned, he received good notices for his work on it. It would be his last role in a television series. Urich's final television film, _Night of the Wolf_, aired on [Animal Planet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_Planet "Animal Planet") the night before his death.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Personal life")]

### Marriages and children

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Marriages and children")]

Urich's first marriage was to actress Barbara Rucker in 1968. They divorced in 1974. He married actress [Heather Menzies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heather_Menzies "Heather Menzies") (1949–2017) in 1975. They adopted three children. They remained married until his death in 2002.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-people-4)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-21)

## Illness and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Illness and death")]

In July 1996, Urich announced his diagnosis with [synovial sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_sarcoma "Synovial sarcoma"), a rare cancer affecting [soft tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_tissue "Soft tissue"). Despite his illness, he continued working, underwent treatment and advocated for cancer cure research. He received an award from the [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne") Cancer Institute and the [Gilda Radner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gilda_Radner "Gilda Radner") Courage Award for his cancer awareness efforts.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-pittsburgh-13) He and his wife established the Urich Fund at the University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center to support cancer research. Additionally, Urich donated $125,000, his winnings from an episode of _[Who Wants to Be a Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Wants\_to\_Be\_a\_Millionaire\_(U.S.\_game\_show) "Who Wants to Be a Millionaire (U.S. game show)")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) He was declared cancer-free in 1998 and became the national spokesperson for the [American Cancer Society](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Cancer_Society "American Cancer Society") that year.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6)

In November 2001, Urich shared in an interview that doctors had found [lumps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor "Tumor") in his body, but a new medication had successfully treated them.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-portsmouth-15) A week before his death, he was hospitalized at [Los Robles Hospital & Medical Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Robles_Hospital_&_Medical_Center "Los Robles Hospital & Medical Center") in [Thousand Oaks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thousand_Oaks,_California "Thousand Oaks, California") with respiratory problems. He died there on April 16, 2002.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-23) His funeral Mass was held on April 19 at [St. Charles Borromeo Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Charles_Borromeo_Church_(North_Hollywood) "St. Charles Borromeo Church (North Hollywood)") in [North Hollywood, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "North Hollywood, Los Angeles").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-cnn-6) A statement was released by his publicist Cindy Guagenti, and said Urich's wife and three children were with him when he died.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes.com-2)

Urich's body was cremated, and his ashes interred at the family's vacation home in [Prince Edward County, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Edward_County,_Ontario "Prince Edward County, Ontario"), Canada. A memorial stands in the West Lake Church of Christ Cemetery, near their vacation home.

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Urich&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Urich and his wife helped to raise money for the Eccles Performing Arts Centers at the [Park City High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City_High_School "Park City High School") in [Park City, Utah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_City,_Utah "Park City, Utah"). After his death, the school established the Robert Urich Scholarship fund in his honor.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-24) In addition, they established the Robert and Heather Urich Fund for Sarcoma Research at the University of Michigan Comprehensive Cancer Center. She also had cancer and was an [ovarian cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cancer "Ovarian cancer") survivor. Heather continued to work for the center, until she died from brain cancer on December 24, 2017, surrounded by their three children.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-25)

Urich's hometown of [Toronto, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto,_Ohio "Toronto, Ohio"), named the Robert Urich Interchange in his honor. It connects the town to [Ohio State Route 7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ohio_State_Route_7 "Ohio State Route 7"). For his contribution to the television industry, Urich has a star on the [Hollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Walk_of_Fame "Hollywood Walk of Fame") located at 7083 Hollywood Boulevard.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-latimes-1) Until [Usher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Usher_(musician) "Usher (musician)") was added, he was the only person with a name starting with the letter U on the walk.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Urich#cite_note-28)

_**Spenser: For Hire**_ is an American [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama") series based on [Robert B. Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_B._Parker "Robert B. Parker")'s _[Spenser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser\_(character) "Spenser (character)")_ novels. The series, developed for TV by [John Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wilder_(producer) "John Wilder (producer)") and starring Robert Urich, was broadcast on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from September 20, 1985, until May 7, 1988.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Production")]

The series ran on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from September 20, 1985, to May 7, 1988. Despite frequent time slot changes and occasional pre-emptions, the show garnered decent ratings. Location shooting ultimately led to the show's demise, with costs being cited as one of the main reasons why ABC cancelled it. Filmed largely in Boston, which was considered one of the show's strong points, it featured shots from many locations, even showing the harsh winters there (notably in the pilot). The show's music was produced by Steve Dorff and Larry Herbstritt.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The series was estimated to have generated $50 million for the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-1)

## Characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Characters")]

### Spenser

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Spenser")]

Spenser (Robert Urich) is the only name used for this character throughout the show. When introducing himself, he often says "Spenser with an 'S', like the [poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Spenser "Edmund Spenser")." In "The Choice", it is revealed that Spenser fared poorly in a professional fight 12 years ago, but he still boxes and exercises at Henry Cimoli's Gym. He is well read, often quoting poetry in everyday conversation, and is an excellent cook, often making recipes he picks up from watching [Julia Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child "Julia Child") on his kitchen counter television.

Spenser lives in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") and drives distinctive cars. His first is a mildly worn-out, dark ivy green 1966 [Ford Mustang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Mustang "Ford Mustang"), with back centered chrome wheels, which is destroyed at the beginning of the second season episode "The Long Hunt". It is succeeded by a new 1987 [Mustang 5.0 GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Mustang_(third_generation)#1987%E2%80%931993 "Ford Mustang (third generation)") which, nine episodes later in "Mary Hamilton", is traded for a perfectly restored dark ivy green 1966 Mustang with Keystone Mags which gets banged up over the remaining run of the show. In the TV films, he drives a red [Ford Probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Probe "Ford Probe") in the first two, then switches to a burgundy red 1967 Ford Mustang fastback for the final two films.

Spenser carries a [Beretta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beretta "Beretta") 9mm pistol and acknowledges being a Vietnam War veteran in the series' pilot episode. Spenser was also a former member of the [Boston police force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Police_Department "Boston Police Department") and occasionally cooperates with the BPD in the series.

In "Children of a Tempest Storm", Susan Silverman ([Barbara Stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Stock "Barbara Stock")) reveals that she is pregnant with Spenser's child. The word _abortion_ comes up when talking with her doctor, and is discussed throughout the episode, though often not using the word. Susan and Spenser discuss the issue and are at odds over the moral dilemma. Spenser, a Catholic, does not know if he can stay with Susan, though he loves her deeply, if she aborts. He believes it is only for her convenience that she would choose abortion. In the end, she has the abortion, and he brings her flowers. They silently affirm that the relationship will continue. After Stock left the show, ADA Rita Fiori ([Carolyn McCormick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_McCormick "Carolyn McCormick")) becomes Spenser's love interest during the second season.

After his apartment goes up in flames in "No Room at the Inn", Spenser moves into a "firehouse", given to him by grateful local firefighters for saving the life of a firefighter at his apartment building. It is situated on the corner of River Street, near Mt. Vernon Square and [Beacon Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beacon_Hill,_Boston "Beacon Hill, Boston"). In the second season, the Fire Department takes the station back and Spenser moves to a small top floor apartment in [Charlestown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlestown,_Boston "Charlestown, Boston"), near the old [Boston Navy Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Navy_Yard "Boston Navy Yard"), which he now uses as his office. The third season finds him in the same apartment and with Susan again, upon her unexpected return.

### Hawk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Hawk")]

Hawk ([Avery Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avery_Brooks "Avery Brooks")) is a smartly dressed, enigmatic enforcer with connections ranging from Beacon Hill to the Boston underworld. Though he is for hire, he has a code of ethics and assists Spenser. In the pilot episode ("Promised Land"), he and Spenser obviously have respect for each other, and he switches over from King Powers' ([Chuck Connors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Connors "Chuck Connors")) side to Spenser's side when he does not like Powers' actions. Hawk carries a [Colt Python .357 Magnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Python "Colt Python") as his weapon of choice.

### Lt. Martin Quirk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Lt. Martin Quirk")]

Lt. Quirk ([Richard Jaeckel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Jaeckel "Richard Jaeckel")) commands the Boston Police major crimes squad. He and Spenser have an uneasy, somewhat adversarial relationship, but often work well together. In the episode "Heart of the Matter", Quirk suffers an [angina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angina "Angina") attack and reluctantly accepts the fact that he must retire after 35 years on the force.

### Sgt. Frank Belson

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Sgt. Frank Belson")]

Sgt. Belson ([Ron McLarty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_McLarty "Ron McLarty")) is Lt. Quirk's right-hand man, one of whose unofficial duties seems to be keeping an eye on Spenser. The overweight Belson is frequently seen eating and his character's role is often to provide comic relief, though he is also shown as being perfectly capable of carrying out serious police work when the occasion demands.

## Episodes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Episodes")]

Main article: [List of Spenser: For Hire episodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Spenser:_For_Hire_episodes "List of Spenser: For Hire episodes")

The series consisted of three seasons (1985–1988) with a total of 66 episodes, and was followed by a series of four made-for-TV movies (1993–1995).

## Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Home media")]

On June 28, 2005, [Rykodisc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rykodisc "Rykodisc") released the four TV movies on DVD that were made following the cancellation of the weekly series.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-2) In 2007, Rykodisc re-released each of them separately.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-3)

| DVD name | Ep # | Additional information |
| --- | --- | --- |
| _Spenser: The Movie Collection_ | 4 | * _Spenser: Ceremony_ * _Spenser: Pale Kings And Princes_ * _Spenser: The Judas Goat_ * _Spenser: A Savage Place_ |

In 2014, [Warner Bros.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Bros. "Warner Bros.") released the first season on DVD via their [Warner Archive Collection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warner_Archive_Collection "Warner Archive Collection"). This is a manufacture-on-demand (MOD) release, available through Warner's online store and Amazon.com. Warner's website explains that the initial disc run was pressed traditionally "to meet expected high consumer demand".[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-4) The second and third seasons were released in 2015,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-5) followed by a box set with all three seasons in 2025.

## Spin-offs and remakes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Spin-offs and remakes")]

In [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_in_television "1989 in television"), after the show ended, Brooks starred in his own spin-off series, _[A Man Called Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Man\_Called\_Hawk "A Man Called Hawk")_.

From 1999 to 2001, [Joe Mantegna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mantegna "Joe Mantegna") played the detective in [a series of three telemovies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser_(film_series) "Spenser (film series)") on A&E.

In an April 23, 2009 blog entry, Robert Parker stated that he was in talks with TNT to produce a remake of the series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-7) However, Parker died in 2010 before these plans could take place.

The 2020 [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") film _[Spenser Confidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser\_Confidential "Spenser Confidential")_ is the first installment of a reboot of the series.

_**Spenser: For Hire**_ is an American [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_drama "Crime drama") series based on [Robert B. Parker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_B._Parker "Robert B. Parker")'s _[Spenser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser\_(character) "Spenser (character)")_ novels. The series, developed for TV by [John Wilder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wilder_(producer) "John Wilder (producer)") and starring Robert Urich, was broadcast on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from September 20, 1985, until May 7, 1988.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Production")]

The series ran on [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") from September 20, 1985, to May 7, 1988. Despite frequent time slot changes and occasional pre-emptions, the show garnered decent ratings. Location shooting ultimately led to the show's demise, with costs being cited as one of the main reasons why ABC cancelled it. Filmed largely in Boston, which was considered one of the show's strong points, it featured shots from many locations, even showing the harsh winters there (notably in the pilot). The show's music was produced by Steve Dorff and Larry Herbstritt.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

The series was estimated to have generated $50 million for the Commonwealth of Massachusetts.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-1)

## Characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Characters")]

### Spenser

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Spenser")]

Spenser (Robert Urich) is the only name used for this character throughout the show. When introducing himself, he often says "Spenser with an 'S', like the [poet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edmund_Spenser "Edmund Spenser")." In "The Choice", it is revealed that Spenser fared poorly in a professional fight 12 years ago, but he still boxes and exercises at Henry Cimoli's Gym. He is well read, often quoting poetry in everyday conversation, and is an excellent cook, often making recipes he picks up from watching [Julia Child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julia_Child "Julia Child") on his kitchen counter television.

Spenser lives in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") and drives distinctive cars. His first is a mildly worn-out, dark ivy green 1966 [Ford Mustang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Mustang "Ford Mustang"), with back centered chrome wheels, which is destroyed at the beginning of the second season episode "The Long Hunt". It is succeeded by a new 1987 [Mustang 5.0 GT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Mustang_(third_generation)#1987%E2%80%931993 "Ford Mustang (third generation)") which, nine episodes later in "Mary Hamilton", is traded for a perfectly restored dark ivy green 1966 Mustang with Keystone Mags which gets banged up over the remaining run of the show. In the TV films, he drives a red [Ford Probe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Probe "Ford Probe") in the first two, then switches to a burgundy red 1967 Ford Mustang fastback for the final two films.

Spenser carries a [Beretta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beretta "Beretta") 9mm pistol and acknowledges being a Vietnam War veteran in the series' pilot episode. Spenser was also a former member of the [Boston police force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Police_Department "Boston Police Department") and occasionally cooperates with the BPD in the series.

In "Children of a Tempest Storm", Susan Silverman ([Barbara Stock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Stock "Barbara Stock")) reveals that she is pregnant with Spenser's child. The word _abortion_ comes up when talking with her doctor, and is discussed throughout the episode, though often not using the word. Susan and Spenser discuss the issue and are at odds over the moral dilemma. Spenser, a Catholic, does not know if he can stay with Susan, though he loves her deeply, if she aborts. He believes it is only for her convenience that she would choose abortion. In the end, she has the abortion, and he brings her flowers. They silently affirm that the relationship will continue. After Stock left the show, ADA Rita Fiori ([Carolyn McCormick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carolyn_McCormick "Carolyn McCormick")) becomes Spenser's love interest during the second season.

After his apartment goes up in flames in "No Room at the Inn", Spenser moves into a "firehouse", given to him by grateful local firefighters for saving the life of a firefighter at his apartment building. It is situated on the corner of River Street, near Mt. Vernon Square and [Beacon Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beacon_Hill,_Boston "Beacon Hill, Boston"). In the second season, the Fire Department takes the station back and Spenser moves to a small top floor apartment in [Charlestown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlestown,_Boston "Charlestown, Boston"), near the old [Boston Navy Yard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Navy_Yard "Boston Navy Yard"), which he now uses as his office. The third season finds him in the same apartment and with Susan again, upon her unexpected return.

### Hawk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Hawk")]

Hawk ([Avery Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avery_Brooks "Avery Brooks")) is a smartly dressed, enigmatic enforcer with connections ranging from Beacon Hill to the Boston underworld. Though he is for hire, he has a code of ethics and assists Spenser. In the pilot episode ("Promised Land"), he and Spenser obviously have respect for each other, and he switches over from King Powers' ([Chuck Connors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuck_Connors "Chuck Connors")) side to Spenser's side when he does not like Powers' actions. Hawk carries a [Colt Python .357 Magnum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Python "Colt Python") as his weapon of choice.

### Lt. Martin Quirk

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Lt. Martin Quirk")]

Lt. Quirk ([Richard Jaeckel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Jaeckel "Richard Jaeckel")) commands the Boston Police major crimes squad. He and Spenser have an uneasy, somewhat adversarial relationship, but often work well together. In the episode "Heart of the Matter", Quirk suffers an [angina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angina "Angina") attack and reluctantly accepts the fact that he must retire after 35 years on the force.

### Sgt. Frank Belson

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Sgt. Frank Belson")]

Sgt. Belson ([Ron McLarty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_McLarty "Ron McLarty")) is Lt. Quirk's right-hand man, one of whose unofficial duties seems to be keeping an eye on Spenser. The overweight Belson is frequently seen eating and his character's role is often to provide comic relief, though he is also shown as being perfectly capable of carrying out serious police work when the occasion demands.

## Episodes

## Spin-offs and remakes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Spenser:_For_Hire&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Spin-offs and remakes")]

In [1989](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1989_in_television "1989 in television"), after the show ended, Brooks starred in his own spin-off series, _[A Man Called Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Man\_Called\_Hawk "A Man Called Hawk")_.

From 1999 to 2001, [Joe Mantegna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Mantegna "Joe Mantegna") played the detective in [a series of three telemovies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser_(film_series) "Spenser (film series)") on A&E.

In an April 23, 2009 blog entry, Robert Parker stated that he was in talks with TNT to produce a remake of the series.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:_For_Hire#cite_note-7) However, Parker died in 2010 before these plans could take place.

The 2020 [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") film _[Spenser Confidential](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser\_Confidential "Spenser Confidential")_ is the first installment of a reboot of the series.

For the made for TV movies starring Joe Mantegna, see [Spenser (TV movies)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser_(TV_movies) "Spenser (TV movies)").

_**[Spenser: For Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spenser:\_For\_Hire "Spenser: For Hire")**_ lasted for three seasons (1985–1988) and was followed by four made-for-TV movies (1993–1995), all starring Robert Urich and [Avery Brooks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avery_Brooks "Avery Brooks").

## TV movies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Spenser:_For_Hire_episodes&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: TV movies")]

During the early 1990s, Urich and Brooks reunited for four made-for-TV films, produced by the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") cable network. The movies were based on four of Parker's novels. Parker and his wife Joan co-wrote the first two screenplays and the two movies kept to the spirit of the series. To keep production costs down Barbara Stock was replaced as Susan Silverman in the first two movies by [Barbara Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Williams_(actress) "Barbara Williams (actress)") and in the other two by veteran actress [Wendy Crewson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Crewson "Wendy Crewson") (_[Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air\_Force\_One\_(film) "Air Force One (film)")_) and Frank Belson was played by J. Winston Carroll. Parker's son Daniel appears in all four movies as a waiter in Spenser's favorite restaurant. Unlike the series which was filmed in Boston, the new movies were filmed in Toronto to take advantage of the lower production costs. The first two movies were still set in Boston (parts of Toronto easily passed for Boston), with the second two rewritten to be set in Toronto (the novel _A Savage Place_ was set in Los Angeles).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

## TV movies

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Spenser:_For_Hire_episodes&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: TV movies")]

During the early 1990s, Urich and Brooks reunited for four made-for-TV films, produced by the [Lifetime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lifetime_(TV_network) "Lifetime (TV network)") cable network. The movies were based on four of Parker's novels. Parker and his wife Joan co-wrote the first two screenplays and the two movies kept to the spirit of the series. To keep production costs down Barbara Stock was replaced as Susan Silverman in the first two movies by [Barbara Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbara_Williams_(actress) "Barbara Williams (actress)") and in the other two by veteran actress [Wendy Crewson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wendy_Crewson "Wendy Crewson") (_[Air Force One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Air\_Force\_One\_(film) "Air Force One (film)")_) and Frank Belson was played by J. Winston Carroll. Parker's son Daniel appears in all four movies as a waiter in Spenser's favorite restaurant. Unlike the series which was filmed in Boston, the new movies were filmed in Toronto to take advantage of the lower production costs. The first two movies were still set in Boston (parts of Toronto easily passed for Boston), with the second two rewritten to be set in Toronto (the novel _A Savage Place_ was set in Los Angeles).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
