**Edward Albert Arthur Woodward** (1 June 1930 – 16 November 2009) was an English actor and singer. He began his career on stage, appearing in productions in both the [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") of London and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). He came to wider attention in the title role of the British television spy drama _[Callan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan\_(TV\_series) "Callan (TV series)")_ (1967–1972), which earned him the 1970 [British Academy Television Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Actor "British Academy Television Award for Best Actor").

Woodward starred as Police Sergeant Neil Howie in the British [folk horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_horror "Folk horror") film _[The Wicker Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wicker\_Man "The Wicker Man")_ (1973) and in the title role of the Australian biopic _[Breaker Morant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaker\_Morant\_(film) "Breaker Morant (film)")_ (1980). From 1985 to 1989, he starred as ex-secret agent turned private investigator Robert McCall in the American television series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_, which earned him the 1986 [Golden Globe Award for Best Television Drama Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Television Series Drama").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Edward Albert Arthur Woodward was born on 1 June 1930 in [Croydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croydon "Croydon"), [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey "Surrey"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-cp-25nov2009-2) the only child of parents Edward Oliver Woodward, a metalworker,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Independent-3) and Violet Edith Woodward (née Smith).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) As a boy, he was bombed out of his home three times during [the Blitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blitz "The Blitz").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1) He attended Eccleston Road, Sydenham Road, as well as [Kingston Day Commercial School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinchley_Wood_School "Hinchley Wood School") and Elmwood High School, Hackbridge, all in Surrey.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Independent-3)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1) He then attended [Kingston College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Thames_Colleges_Group "South Thames Colleges Group").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-cp-25nov2009-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5)

After leaving school at the age of 15, Woodward wanted to train as a journalist, but took work in a [sanitary engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanitary_engineering "Sanitary engineering")'s office, and then at the age of 16 entered the [Royal Academy of Dramatic Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academy_of_Dramatic_Art "Royal Academy of Dramatic Art") (RADA) as their youngest ever student.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Theatre")]

Woodward's professional acting debut was in the Castle Theatre, [Farnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farnham "Farnham"), in 1946.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6) He started worked extensively in [repertory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repertory "Repertory") companies as a Shakespearean actor, making his London stage debut in [R. F. Delderfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._F._Delderfield "R. F. Delderfield")'s _Where There's a Will_ in 1955[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6) and also appeared in [the film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_There's_a_Will_(1955_film) "Where There's a Will (1955 film)") that same year, his first film, and then _[Romeo and Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo\_and\_Juliet "Romeo and Juliet")_ and _[Hamlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamlet "Hamlet")_ (1955).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) Having established himself, he also worked in Broadway theatre in New York City and in Australia. Woodward first appeared on Broadway in _Rattle of a Simple Man_ (1963) and the musical comedy _[High Spirits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Spirits\_(musical) "High Spirits (musical)")_ (1964–1965),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) which won three [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards"), followed by the 1966 comedy _The Best Laid Plans_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) In 1970, after Woodward played Sidney Carton in the West End musical _Two Cities_, based on Dickens's novel _[A Tale of Two Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Tale\_of\_Two\_Cities "A Tale of Two Cities")_, [Laurence Olivier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier "Laurence Olivier") invited him to choose his own role in the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre"), and he chose _[Cyrano de Bergerac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrano\_de\_Bergerac\_(play) "Cyrano de Bergerac (play)")_ (1971).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6)

Woodward played [Dr. Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Watson "Dr. Watson") opposite [Keith Baxter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Baxter_(actor) "Keith Baxter (actor)") as [Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock_Holmes "Sherlock Holmes") in the play _Murder Dear Watson_ in 1983.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-7)

In 2004, Woodward, alongside Australian actor [Daniel MacPherson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_MacPherson "Daniel MacPherson"), appeared as God in a revival of [_The Mystery Plays_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mysteries "The Mysteries") at [Canterbury Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury_Cathedral "Canterbury Cathedral").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) From a cast of hundreds of local actors, [Joseph McManners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McManners "Joseph McManners") and [Thomas James Longley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_James_Longley "Thomas James Longley") also featured with smaller speaking roles.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Mysteries-8)

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Film")]

Woodward made occasional film appearances before taking the lead role of Police Sergeant Neil Howie in the [folk horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_horror "Folk horror") film _The Wicker Man_ (1973). [Robin Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Hardy_(film_director) "Robin Hardy (film director)"), who directed the film, said, "He was one of the greatest actors of his generation, without a doubt, with a broad career on American television, as well as on British film."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-9) He was offered a [cameo role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_role "Cameo role") in the remake, _[The Wicker Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wicker\_Man\_(2006\_film) "The Wicker Man (2006 film)")_ (2006), but declined. He also appeared as Commander Powell in the 1982 film _[Who Dares Wins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Dares\_Wins\_(film) "Who Dares Wins (film)")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

Woodward played the title role in the 1980 Australian biographical film drama _Breaker Morant_,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) and had a supporting role in the 2007 action comedy _[Hot Fuzz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot\_Fuzz "Hot Fuzz")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) His last lead film role was that of the story of an eccentric vicar Reverend Frederick Densham in _A Congregation of Ghosts_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

In 1990, Woodward was the narrator for the official FIFA film of the [1990 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_World_Cup "1990 World Cup") entitled _Soccer Shoot-Out_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

[Noël Coward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No%C3%ABl_Coward "Noël Coward") once said Woodward was "one of the nicest and most co-operative actors I've ever met or worked with."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Television")]

Woodward appeared in many television productions. In the early 1960s, he was a jobbing actor who made a number of minor TV appearances in supporting roles. His casting as Guy Crouchback, the central character in Waugh's three novels set against the background of Britain's involvement in World War II, in the 1967 adaption of [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s _[Sword of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Honour "Sword of Honour")_ trilogy, dramatised by [Giles Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giles_Cooper_(playwright) "Giles Cooper (playwright)") and directed by [Donald McWhinnie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_McWhinnie "Donald McWhinnie") established him. That black-and-white TV dramatisation was remade in 2001 in a colour version with [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig") playing the part of Crouchback. The 1967 _Sword_ featured several leading actors of that era, including [Ronald Fraser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Fraser_(actor) "Ronald Fraser (actor)"), [Freddie Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Jones "Freddie Jones"), [Vivian Pickles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Pickles "Vivian Pickles"), [Nicholas Courtney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Courtney "Nicholas Courtney"), and [James Villiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Villiers "James Villiers"). Evelyn Waugh had met and approved Giles Cooper as the scriptwriter, having their schooling at [Lancing College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancing_College "Lancing College") in common, albeit more than a decade apart.

In 1967, Woodward played the eventual victim in the episode "The Persistent Patriots" of _[The Saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Saint\_(TV\_series) "The Saint (TV series)")_ TV series.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) The same year, he was cast as David Callan in the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)")_[Armchair Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armchair\_Theatre "Armchair Theatre")_ play _A Magnum for Schneider_, which later became the spy series _[Callan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan\_(TV\_series) "Callan (TV series)")_, one of his early television roles. His performance assured the series' success from 1967 to 1972, with a [film appearing in 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan_(film) "Callan (film)"). He appeared opposite Laurence Olivier in a 1978 adaptation of _Saturday, Sunday, Monday_ in the _[Laurence Olivier Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence\_Olivier\_Presents "Laurence Olivier Presents")_ anthology TV series.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

_Callan_ made Woodward one of the most popular actors in Britain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-joseph1980-10) The show typecast him somewhat, but the enduring success of the genre allowed him to gain leading roles in similar productions, though none would prove to be as iconic as _Callan_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-11)[Michael C. Burgess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_C._Burgess_(editor) "Michael C. Burgess (editor)") of Cinemalogue said, "of his more than 2,000 television performances, his portrayal of the ex-SIS undercover man Callan created an icon, if not a genre."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-12) In 1977, he starred in two series of the [BBC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC2 "BBC2") dystopian drama _[1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990\_(TV\_series) "1990 (TV series)")_, about a future Britain lurching into [totalitarianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totalitarianism "Totalitarianism").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-13)

In the mid 1980s, Woodward took the lead role in the American television series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_ (1985–1989) as a former intelligence operative. After filming a few episodes of the third season, Woodward suffered a massive [coronary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myocardial_infarction "Myocardial infarction"). For several episodes, additional actors were brought in to reduce the workload on Woodward as he recovered from the condition. The first episode, filmed following Woodward's heart attack, involved his character being severely injured by a [KGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KGB "KGB") bullet, providing Woodward with a chance to rest over several episodes. Later in the season, Woodward resumed his full duties and carried the show through a fourth season during 1988–1989.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] During this period, he also starred in the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") espionage thriller, _[Codename: Kyril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codename:\_Kyril "Codename: Kyril")_ (1988), as an [MI6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI6 "MI6") double agent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

Subsequently, he starred in the short-lived CBS series _[Over My Dead Body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over\_My\_Dead\_Body\_(TV\_series) "Over My Dead Body (TV series)")_, which ran in 1990, playing a mystery writer who gets involved in solving real crimes. In 1994 and 1997, Woodward starred in the BBC drama _[Common As Muck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common\_As\_Muck "Common As Muck")_, in which he played a binman called Nev.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

In 1993, Woodward appeared in the [Welsh language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_language "Welsh language") drama, _Tan ar y Comin_. Versions were made in both English and Welsh, and Woodward appeared in both, being specially coached in the latter, since he did not speak a word of the language.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-14)

In 1999, Woodward appeared alongside his son [Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Woodward "Peter Woodward") in "The Long Road", an episode of the _[Babylon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylon\_5 "Babylon 5")_ spin-off, _[Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusade\_(TV\_series) "Crusade (TV series)")_, on which Peter was a regular cast member.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Both actors were playing the part of unrelated [Technomages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technomage_(Babylon_5) "Technomage (Babylon 5)").

His career continued with TV guest-star roles, including an appearance in _[The New Alfred Hitchcock Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Alfred\_Hitchcock\_Presents "The New Alfred Hitchcock Presents")_ and Mr. Jones (or Philip, codename Flavius) in the series _[La Femme Nikita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Femme\_Nikita\_(TV\_series) "La Femme Nikita (TV series)")_. He also guest-starred with his son [Tim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Woodward "Tim Woodward") and grandson Sam as a London gangster family in a special storyline for _[The Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bill "The Bill")_ in 2008. In March 2009, he joined _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ for six episodes, playing [Tommy Clifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Clifford "Tommy Clifford").

Woodward was a [wargamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wargame "Wargame") and hosted a six episode television series, called _Battleground_, for [Tyne Tees Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyne_Tees_Television "Tyne Tees Television")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-15) in 1978 about the hobby, with fellow enthusiast Peter Gilder, who built and owned the beautiful Gettysburg diorama used for one of the gaming scenes for the 1974 film _Callan_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-17)

Woodward was the subject of _[This Is Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_Your\_Life\_(British\_TV\_series) "This Is Your Life (British TV series)")_ on two occasions; in February 1971, he was surprised by [Eamonn Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eamonn_Andrews "Eamonn Andrews") in the bar of London's White House Hotel,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and in February 1995, [Michael Aspel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Aspel "Michael Aspel") surprised him during a photoshoot at Syon House in West London.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music")]

Woodward's capability as [tenor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenor "Tenor") enabled him to record 12 albums of romantic songs, and three albums of poetry and 14 books to tape. His vocal ability and acting skill enabled him to make a number of appearances when time allowed on the BBC's [Edwardian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwardian_era "Edwardian era")[music hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_hall "Music hall") programme, _[The Good Old Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Old\_Days\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Good Old Days (UK TV series)")_.

Woodward had two top-100 albums in the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"); _This Man Alone_ (number 53 in 1970) and _The Edward Woodward Album_ (number 20 in 1972), while the single "The Way You Look Tonight" peaked at number 42 on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") in 1971.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-18) He also had two top-100 albums in Australia; _Edwardian Woodward_ (number 97 in 1975) and _A Romantic Hour_ (#92 in 1980)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-aus-19)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Woodward was married twice. His first marriage was to actress Venetia Barrett (born Venetia Mary Collett, 1928–2016) from 1952 to 1986.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5) They had two sons: [Tim Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Woodward "Tim Woodward") (1953–2023) and [Peter Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Woodward "Peter Woodward") (born 1956), both of whom became actors, as well as a daughter, [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards")-nominated actress [Sarah Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Woodward "Sarah Woodward") (born 1963). Woodward left Barrett for actress [Michele Dotrice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Dotrice "Michele Dotrice"), the daughter of his contemporary [Roy Dotrice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Dotrice "Roy Dotrice"), and married her in New York City in January 1987. Their daughter, Emily Beth Woodward (born 1983),[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] was present at the ceremony.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-20)

In 1974, Woodward was present during the [Turkish invasion of Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus "Turkish invasion of Cyprus"). Staying in the northern town of [Kyrenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrenia "Kyrenia"), he was one of several Britons evacuated from the island by the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") aircraft carrier [HMS _Hermes_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hermes_(R12) "HMS Hermes (R12)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-21)

Woodward was a prominent endorser of the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_(UK) "Labour Party (UK)") in the [1970 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_United_Kingdom_general_election "1970 United Kingdom general election"), featuring in publicity material.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-22) He later declared his support for the [Social Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_(UK) "Social Democratic Party (UK)") (SDP).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Woodward suffered a massive heart attack in 1987 (during the third season of _The Equalizer_) and another one in 1994. He underwent [triple-bypass surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_bypass_surgery "Coronary artery bypass surgery") in 1996 and quit smoking. In 2003, he was diagnosed with [prostate cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prostate_cancer "Prostate cancer").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-23) In July 2009, a planned performance of _[Love Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Letters\_(play) "Love Letters (play)")_ (1988), co-starring his wife Michele, was to be postponed because of damage caused to his hip when he fell down the stairs at his [West Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Country "West Country") home.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-mirr_Edwa-24)

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Death")]

Woodward died of pneumonia at the [Royal Cornwall Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Cornwall_Hospital "Royal Cornwall Hospital") in [Truro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truro "Truro"), Cornwall, on 16 November 2009, at the age of 79, near his home at [Hawker's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker's_Cove,_Cornwall "Hawker's Cove, Cornwall").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-27)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Awards")]

Woodward won the 1970 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") Award for Best Actor for his title role in _Callan_. He was made an [Officer of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (OBE) in 1978. At the 1987 [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), he won Best Actor in a Dramatic TV Series for his role of Robert McCall in _The Equalizer_. At the [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") from 1986 to 1990, he was nominated each year for _The Equalizer_.

*   [British Academy Television Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Actor "British Academy Television Award for Best Actor") – 1970
*   RTS Television Actor of the Year – 1969, 1970

*   [Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Drama Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primetime_Emmy_Award_for_Outstanding_Guest_Actor_in_a_Drama_Series "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Guest Actor in a Drama Series") (nominated) – 1989

**Edward Albert Arthur Woodward** (1 June 1930 – 16 November 2009) was an English actor and singer. He began his career on stage, appearing in productions in both the [West End](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_End_theatre "West End theatre") of London and on [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). He came to wider attention in the title role of the British television spy drama _[Callan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan\_(TV\_series) "Callan (TV series)")_ (1967–1972), which earned him the 1970 [British Academy Television Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Actor "British Academy Television Award for Best Actor").

Woodward starred as Police Sergeant Neil Howie in the British [folk horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_horror "Folk horror") film _[The Wicker Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wicker\_Man "The Wicker Man")_ (1973) and in the title role of the Australian biopic _[Breaker Morant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breaker\_Morant\_(film) "Breaker Morant (film)")_ (1980). From 1985 to 1989, he starred as ex-secret agent turned private investigator Robert McCall in the American television series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_, which earned him the 1986 [Golden Globe Award for Best Television Drama Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Television_Series_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Television Series Drama").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Edward Albert Arthur Woodward was born on 1 June 1930 in [Croydon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croydon "Croydon"), [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey "Surrey"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-cp-25nov2009-2) the only child of parents Edward Oliver Woodward, a metalworker,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Independent-3) and Violet Edith Woodward (née Smith).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) As a boy, he was bombed out of his home three times during [the Blitz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Blitz "The Blitz").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1) He attended Eccleston Road, Sydenham Road, as well as [Kingston Day Commercial School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hinchley_Wood_School "Hinchley Wood School") and Elmwood High School, Hackbridge, all in Surrey.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Independent-3)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1) He then attended [Kingston College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Thames_Colleges_Group "South Thames Colleges Group").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-IT-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-cp-25nov2009-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5)

After leaving school at the age of 15, Woodward wanted to train as a journalist, but took work in a [sanitary engineer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanitary_engineering "Sanitary engineering")'s office, and then at the age of 16 entered the [Royal Academy of Dramatic Art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Academy_of_Dramatic_Art "Royal Academy of Dramatic Art") (RADA) as their youngest ever student.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Theatre

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Theatre")]

Woodward's professional acting debut was in the Castle Theatre, [Farnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farnham "Farnham"), in 1946.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6) He started worked extensively in [repertory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Repertory "Repertory") companies as a Shakespearean actor, making his London stage debut in [R. F. Delderfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/R._F._Delderfield "R. F. Delderfield")'s _Where There's a Will_ in 1955[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6) and also appeared in [the film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Where_There's_a_Will_(1955_film) "Where There's a Will (1955 film)") that same year, his first film, and then _[Romeo and Juliet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romeo\_and\_Juliet "Romeo and Juliet")_ and _[Hamlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamlet "Hamlet")_ (1955).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) Having established himself, he also worked in Broadway theatre in New York City and in Australia. Woodward first appeared on Broadway in _Rattle of a Simple Man_ (1963) and the musical comedy _[High Spirits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High\_Spirits\_(musical) "High Spirits (musical)")_ (1964–1965),[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) which won three [Tony Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards"), followed by the 1966 comedy _The Best Laid Plans_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) In 1970, after Woodward played Sidney Carton in the West End musical _Two Cities_, based on Dickens's novel _[A Tale of Two Cities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Tale\_of\_Two\_Cities "A Tale of Two Cities")_, [Laurence Olivier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Olivier "Laurence Olivier") invited him to choose his own role in the [Royal National Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_National_Theatre "Royal National Theatre"), and he chose _[Cyrano de Bergerac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyrano\_de\_Bergerac\_(play) "Cyrano de Bergerac (play)")_ (1971).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-BBCObituary-6)

Woodward played [Dr. Watson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dr._Watson "Dr. Watson") opposite [Keith Baxter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Baxter_(actor) "Keith Baxter (actor)") as [Sherlock Holmes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherlock_Holmes "Sherlock Holmes") in the play _Murder Dear Watson_ in 1983.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-7)

In 2004, Woodward, alongside Australian actor [Daniel MacPherson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_MacPherson "Daniel MacPherson"), appeared as God in a revival of [_The Mystery Plays_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mysteries "The Mysteries") at [Canterbury Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canterbury_Cathedral "Canterbury Cathedral").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) From a cast of hundreds of local actors, [Joseph McManners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McManners "Joseph McManners") and [Thomas James Longley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_James_Longley "Thomas James Longley") also featured with smaller speaking roles.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-Mysteries-8)

### Film

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Film")]

Woodward made occasional film appearances before taking the lead role of Police Sergeant Neil Howie in the [folk horror](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Folk_horror "Folk horror") film _The Wicker Man_ (1973). [Robin Hardy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robin_Hardy_(film_director) "Robin Hardy (film director)"), who directed the film, said, "He was one of the greatest actors of his generation, without a doubt, with a broad career on American television, as well as on British film."[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-9) He was offered a [cameo role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_role "Cameo role") in the remake, _[The Wicker Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wicker\_Man\_(2006\_film) "The Wicker Man (2006 film)")_ (2006), but declined. He also appeared as Commander Powell in the 1982 film _[Who Dares Wins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Who\_Dares\_Wins\_(film) "Who Dares Wins (film)")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

Woodward played the title role in the 1980 Australian biographical film drama _Breaker Morant_,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) and had a supporting role in the 2007 action comedy _[Hot Fuzz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot\_Fuzz "Hot Fuzz")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) His last lead film role was that of the story of an eccentric vicar Reverend Frederick Densham in _A Congregation of Ghosts_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

In 1990, Woodward was the narrator for the official FIFA film of the [1990 World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990_World_Cup "1990 World Cup") entitled _Soccer Shoot-Out_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

[Noël Coward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No%C3%ABl_Coward "Noël Coward") once said Woodward was "one of the nicest and most co-operative actors I've ever met or worked with."[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5)

### Television

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Television")]

Woodward appeared in many television productions. In the early 1960s, he was a jobbing actor who made a number of minor TV appearances in supporting roles. His casting as Guy Crouchback, the central character in Waugh's three novels set against the background of Britain's involvement in World War II, in the 1967 adaption of [Evelyn Waugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evelyn_Waugh "Evelyn Waugh")'s _[Sword of Honour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sword\_of\_Honour "Sword of Honour")_ trilogy, dramatised by [Giles Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giles_Cooper_(playwright) "Giles Cooper (playwright)") and directed by [Donald McWhinnie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_McWhinnie "Donald McWhinnie") established him. That black-and-white TV dramatisation was remade in 2001 in a colour version with [Daniel Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Craig "Daniel Craig") playing the part of Crouchback. The 1967 _Sword_ featured several leading actors of that era, including [Ronald Fraser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Fraser_(actor) "Ronald Fraser (actor)"), [Freddie Jones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Jones "Freddie Jones"), [Vivian Pickles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vivian_Pickles "Vivian Pickles"), [Nicholas Courtney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicholas_Courtney "Nicholas Courtney"), and [James Villiers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Villiers "James Villiers"). Evelyn Waugh had met and approved Giles Cooper as the scriptwriter, having their schooling at [Lancing College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancing_College "Lancing College") in common, albeit more than a decade apart.

In 1967, Woodward played the eventual victim in the episode "The Persistent Patriots" of _[The Saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Saint\_(TV\_series) "The Saint (TV series)")_ TV series.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4) The same year, he was cast as David Callan in the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)")_[Armchair Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armchair\_Theatre "Armchair Theatre")_ play _A Magnum for Schneider_, which later became the spy series _[Callan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan\_(TV\_series) "Callan (TV series)")_, one of his early television roles. His performance assured the series' success from 1967 to 1972, with a [film appearing in 1974](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callan_(film) "Callan (film)"). He appeared opposite Laurence Olivier in a 1978 adaptation of _Saturday, Sunday, Monday_ in the _[Laurence Olivier Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence\_Olivier\_Presents "Laurence Olivier Presents")_ anthology TV series.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

_Callan_ made Woodward one of the most popular actors in Britain.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-joseph1980-10) The show typecast him somewhat, but the enduring success of the genre allowed him to gain leading roles in similar productions, though none would prove to be as iconic as _Callan_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-11)[Michael C. Burgess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_C._Burgess_(editor) "Michael C. Burgess (editor)") of Cinemalogue said, "of his more than 2,000 television performances, his portrayal of the ex-SIS undercover man Callan created an icon, if not a genre."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-12) In 1977, he starred in two series of the [BBC2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC2 "BBC2") dystopian drama _[1990](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1990\_(TV\_series) "1990 (TV series)")_, about a future Britain lurching into [totalitarianism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Totalitarianism "Totalitarianism").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-13)

In the mid 1980s, Woodward took the lead role in the American television series _[The Equalizer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_(1985\_TV\_series) "The Equalizer (1985 TV series)")_ (1985–1989) as a former intelligence operative. After filming a few episodes of the third season, Woodward suffered a massive [coronary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myocardial_infarction "Myocardial infarction"). For several episodes, additional actors were brought in to reduce the workload on Woodward as he recovered from the condition. The first episode, filmed following Woodward's heart attack, involved his character being severely injured by a [KGB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KGB "KGB") bullet, providing Woodward with a chance to rest over several episodes. Later in the season, Woodward resumed his full duties and carried the show through a fourth season during 1988–1989.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] During this period, he also starred in the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War") espionage thriller, _[Codename: Kyril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codename:\_Kyril "Codename: Kyril")_ (1988), as an [MI6](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MI6 "MI6") double agent.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

Subsequently, he starred in the short-lived CBS series _[Over My Dead Body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Over\_My\_Dead\_Body\_(TV\_series) "Over My Dead Body (TV series)")_, which ran in 1990, playing a mystery writer who gets involved in solving real crimes. In 1994 and 1997, Woodward starred in the BBC drama _[Common As Muck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common\_As\_Muck "Common As Muck")_, in which he played a binman called Nev.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-film-4)

In 1993, Woodward appeared in the [Welsh language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_language "Welsh language") drama, _Tan ar y Comin_. Versions were made in both English and Welsh, and Woodward appeared in both, being specially coached in the latter, since he did not speak a word of the language.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-14)

In 1999, Woodward appeared alongside his son [Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Woodward "Peter Woodward") in "The Long Road", an episode of the _[Babylon 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylon\_5 "Babylon 5")_ spin-off, _[Crusade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crusade\_(TV\_series) "Crusade (TV series)")_, on which Peter was a regular cast member.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Both actors were playing the part of unrelated [Technomages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technomage_(Babylon_5) "Technomage (Babylon 5)").

His career continued with TV guest-star roles, including an appearance in _[The New Alfred Hitchcock Presents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_New\_Alfred\_Hitchcock\_Presents "The New Alfred Hitchcock Presents")_ and Mr. Jones (or Philip, codename Flavius) in the series _[La Femme Nikita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Femme\_Nikita\_(TV\_series) "La Femme Nikita (TV series)")_. He also guest-starred with his son [Tim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Woodward "Tim Woodward") and grandson Sam as a London gangster family in a special storyline for _[The Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bill "The Bill")_ in 2008. In March 2009, he joined _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ for six episodes, playing [Tommy Clifford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Clifford "Tommy Clifford").

Woodward was a [wargamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wargame "Wargame") and hosted a six episode television series, called _Battleground_, for [Tyne Tees Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyne_Tees_Television "Tyne Tees Television")[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-15) in 1978 about the hobby, with fellow enthusiast Peter Gilder, who built and owned the beautiful Gettysburg diorama used for one of the gaming scenes for the 1974 film _Callan_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-17)

Woodward was the subject of _[This Is Your Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Is\_Your\_Life\_(British\_TV\_series) "This Is Your Life (British TV series)")_ on two occasions; in February 1971, he was surprised by [Eamonn Andrews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eamonn_Andrews "Eamonn Andrews") in the bar of London's White House Hotel,[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] and in February 1995, [Michael Aspel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Aspel "Michael Aspel") surprised him during a photoshoot at Syon House in West London.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Music")]

Woodward's capability as [tenor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tenor "Tenor") enabled him to record 12 albums of romantic songs, and three albums of poetry and 14 books to tape. His vocal ability and acting skill enabled him to make a number of appearances when time allowed on the BBC's [Edwardian era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwardian_era "Edwardian era")[music hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_hall "Music hall") programme, _[The Good Old Days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Good\_Old\_Days\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Good Old Days (UK TV series)")_.

Woodward had two top-100 albums in the [UK Albums Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart"); _This Man Alone_ (number 53 in 1970) and _The Edward Woodward Album_ (number 20 in 1972), while the single "The Way You Look Tonight" peaked at number 42 on the [UK singles chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UK_singles_chart "UK singles chart") in 1971.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-18) He also had two top-100 albums in Australia; _Edwardian Woodward_ (number 97 in 1975) and _A Romantic Hour_ (#92 in 1980)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-aus-19)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Woodward was married twice. His first marriage was to actress Venetia Barrett (born Venetia Mary Collett, 1928–2016) from 1952 to 1986.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-telegraphobit-5) They had two sons: [Tim Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tim_Woodward "Tim Woodward") (1953–2023) and [Peter Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Woodward "Peter Woodward") (born 1956), both of whom became actors, as well as a daughter, [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Awards "Tony Awards")-nominated actress [Sarah Woodward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarah_Woodward "Sarah Woodward") (born 1963). Woodward left Barrett for actress [Michele Dotrice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michele_Dotrice "Michele Dotrice"), the daughter of his contemporary [Roy Dotrice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roy_Dotrice "Roy Dotrice"), and married her in New York City in January 1987. Their daughter, Emily Beth Woodward (born 1983),[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] was present at the ceremony.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-20)

In 1974, Woodward was present during the [Turkish invasion of Cyprus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkish_invasion_of_Cyprus "Turkish invasion of Cyprus"). Staying in the northern town of [Kyrenia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyrenia "Kyrenia"), he was one of several Britons evacuated from the island by the [Royal Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Navy "Royal Navy") aircraft carrier [HMS _Hermes_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HMS_Hermes_(R12) "HMS Hermes (R12)").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-21)

Woodward was a prominent endorser of the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labour_Party_(UK) "Labour Party (UK)") in the [1970 general election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970_United_Kingdom_general_election "1970 United Kingdom general election"), featuring in publicity material.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-22) He later declared his support for the [Social Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_Democratic_Party_(UK) "Social Democratic Party (UK)") (SDP).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Woodward suffered a massive heart attack in 1987 (during the third season of _The Equalizer_) and another one in 1994. He underwent [triple-bypass surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_bypass_surgery "Coronary artery bypass surgery") in 1996 and quit smoking. In 2003, he was diagnosed with [prostate cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prostate_cancer "Prostate cancer").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-23) In July 2009, a planned performance of _[Love Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love\_Letters\_(play) "Love Letters (play)")_ (1988), co-starring his wife Michele, was to be postponed because of damage caused to his hip when he fell down the stairs at his [West Country](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Country "West Country") home.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-mirr_Edwa-24)

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Death")]

Woodward died of pneumonia at the [Royal Cornwall Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Cornwall_Hospital "Royal Cornwall Hospital") in [Truro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truro "Truro"), Cornwall, on 16 November 2009, at the age of 79, near his home at [Hawker's Cove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawker's_Cove,_Cornwall "Hawker's Cove, Cornwall").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Woodward#cite_note-27)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Edward_Woodward&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Awards")]

Woodward won the 1970 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") Award for Best Actor for his title role in _Callan_. He was made an [Officer of the Order of the British Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_the_British_Empire "Order of the British Empire") (OBE) in 1978. At the 1987 [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"), he won Best Actor in a Dramatic TV Series for his role of Robert McCall in _The Equalizer_. At the [Emmy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmy_Award "Emmy Award") from 1986 to 1990, he was nominated each year for _The Equalizer_.

_**The Equalizer**_ is an American [action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film")[crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime "Crime")[drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") television series, originally airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") from September 18, 1985, to August 24, 1989, which was co-created by [Michael Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sloan_(television_writer) "Michael Sloan (television writer)") and [Richard Lindheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Lindheim "Richard Lindheim"). It starred the English actor Edward Woodward as Robert McCall, a retired intelligence agent with a mysterious past, who uses the skills from his former career to exact justice on behalf of innocent people who find themselves in dangerous circumstances, while sometimes also dealing with people from his past in covert operations who want to pull him back in or settle old scores. In the years after its cancellation, the show has received a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-CultRant-1) that inspired further works, including [three feature films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#Film_series) and a [re-imagined series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(2021_TV_series) "The Equalizer (2021 TV series)").

## Series plot elements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Series plot elements")]

The series stars British actor Edward Woodward as Robert McCall, a former [covert operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covert_operations "Covert operations") officer of an unnamed American government intelligence organization, which was often referred to simply as "the Agency" or "the Company", who tries to atone for his past by offering, usually free of charge, his services as a troubleshooter, a protector, and an investigator.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer01-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)

People in need found him through a newspaper [classified ad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classified_ad "Classified ad"): "Got a problem? Odds against you? Call the Equalizer: 212 555 4200."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer04-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5) When he began the business in the pilot episode, the nickname "Equalizer" was revealed as bestowed on him by an operative named "Brahms", played by [Jerry Stiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Stiller "Jerry Stiller").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)

Aided by a group of sometimes mysterious contacts, some of whom date back to his spying days, McCall traverses the streets of [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), delivering justice upon bullies, corrupt police officials and politicians, hoodlums, mobsters, rapists, racists, murderers, kidnappers, drug dealers, and other "truly deserving" people. "Please don't do anything you will never live to regret," he tells one villain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer06-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-7)

His contacts were also prone to human foibles that ranged from egoism to domestic problems.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5)

Many episodes focused on McCall interacting with "Control" (played by [Robert Lansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lansing_(actor) "Robert Lansing (actor)")), the unnamed head of the Manhattan office of the secret organization for which McCall used to work.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3) As a general rule, however, the people responding to the newspaper ad were unremarkable, average, and unknown.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer03-8)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer06-6)

McCall's [Jaguar XJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaguar_XJ "Jaguar XJ")[saloon car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saloon_car "Saloon car"), weapons, and other gadgetry at times featured significantly as elements in the plot.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5)

## Cast and characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast and characters")]

### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   Edward Woodward as Robert McCall: A veteran operative of The Company who becomes disillusioned with sacrificing ordinary people for the perceived greater good. He quits and takes out a newspaper advert offering his services to those who need it as The Equalizer. McCall himself is divorced, a "lost dad" long estranged from his son, Scott ([William Zabka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Zabka "William Zabka")). Woodward was nominated for an Emmy for Outstanding Actor in a Drama Series four years in a row but never won, and was also nominated in 1986 and 1987 for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Television Series Drama, winning in 1986.
*   [Keith Szarabajka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Szarabajka "Keith Szarabajka") as Michael "Mickey" Kostmayer (Also starring, 56 episodes): a former [Navy SEAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_SEAL "Navy SEAL"), who was thrown in the brig for a crime he did not commit, until McCall cleared him and recommended he join The Company. He is often utilized to surveil suspects and protect clients and witnesses.

### Notable guest stars

## Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Music")]

The show's theme music was created by composer/performer [Stewart Copeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_Copeland "Stewart Copeland"). The track is called "Busy Equalizing". An extended version appears on his album _The Equalizer and Other Cliff Hangers._

Six episodes in the 1988 season were scored by [Joseph Conlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Conlan "Joseph Conlan") and the final season was scored by [Cameron Allan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Allan "Cameron Allan"). Other episodes were scored by [John Cacavas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cacavas "John Cacavas").

The show ran for four seasons of 22 episodes each. It was initially renewed for a fifth season (causing Keith Szarabajka to turn down a role on _[Midnight Caller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Caller "Midnight Caller")_). However, the show was later canceled due to a row between CBS and Universal Studios over the renewal of _[Murder, She Wrote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder,\_She\_Wrote "Murder, She Wrote")_.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-DVDTcomcol-74)

In _The Story of The Equalizer_, created for the DVD box set, executive producer Coleman Luck also stated that Universal requested a script for a [crossover episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_episode "Crossover episode") with _[Magnum, P.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum,\_P.I. "Magnum, P.I.")_ despite the objections of the _Equalizer_ crew as its dark tone was much different than _Magnum_'s much lighter and sunnier style. Ultimately the episode was never filmed, but its script was adapted and changed, airing as the episode "Beyond Control".

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Critical response")]

After the broadcast of the first episode in September 1985, the show received mixed reviews. Critic [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") wrote in _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ that "to judge from this very attractively atmospheric premiere, [the show] could become a welcome guest in many an American home".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-87) However, for _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_, [Jeff Jarvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarvis "Jeff Jarvis") wrote, "The plot’s confusing and the show's as erratic as a [pacemaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacemaker "Pacemaker") on low batteries".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-88)

## Localizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Localizations")]

The series was translated into [Afrikaans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaans "Afrikaans") for broadcast through South Africa's [SABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SABC "SABC") as _Die laaste uitweg_.

The series was broadcast throughout the Arab World with Arabic subtitles during the 1990s, like in Egypt through [Channel 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Egypt "Television in Egypt") and Saudi Arabia through [Saudi 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_2 "Saudi 2").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-93)

## Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Home media")]

On February 12, 2008, [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Home_Entertainment "Universal Studios Home Entertainment") released Season 1 of _The Equalizer_ on [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD-Video "DVD-Video") in Region 1 (US only).[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs1-94)

On May 15, 2013, it was announced that [Visual Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Entertainment "Visual Entertainment") had acquired the rights to the series in Region 1.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDplan-95) They subsequently released season 2 on DVD on August 26, 2014.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs3-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs2-97) Season 3 was released on October 25, 2014, followed by season 4 on November 24, 2014.

[Visual Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Entertainment "Visual Entertainment") also released a limited edition complete series set on DVD on August 19, 2014.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-VisualEntertainment.tv-98)_The Equalizer Complete Collection Limited Edition_ set contains all 88 episodes plus 12 hours of bonus content including _[CI5: The New Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CI5:\_The\_New\_Professionals "CI5: The New Professionals")_; the last film ever done by Edward Woodward, _A Congregation of Ghosts_; and _The Story of The Equalizer_ featuring interviews with cast and crew.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-VisualEntertainment.tv-98)

In Region 2, Universal Playback UK released season 1 on DVD on April 21, 2008. In late 2011, Fabulous Films announced that they had acquired the rights to the series. They have subsequently released seasons 2–4.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-FabFilms-99) On May 27, 2013, Fabulous Films released _The Equalizer: The Complete Collection_ on DVD.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-FabFilmsCC-100) This 24-disc box set contains all 88 episodes of the series as well as bonus content including an all-new documentary featuring interviews with cast and crew.

For the Region 1 DVD's many of the music apart from the theme and scoring by Stewart Copeland has been replaced by cover versions due to the costs for music licensing. In contrast, the Region 2 version contains all of the original music intact.

In Region 4, Umbrella Entertainment has released all four seasons on DVD in Australia.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Umbrel4-101)

## Adaptations

### Film series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Film series")]

Main articles: [The Equalizer (film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(film) "The Equalizer (film)"), [The Equalizer 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_2 "The Equalizer 2"), and [The Equalizer 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_3 "The Equalizer 3")

A film starring [Denzel Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Washington "Denzel Washington") in the title role, very loosely based upon the series, was released in September 2014. It was followed by a sequel, _[The Equalizer 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_2 "The Equalizer 2")_, which was released on July 20, 2018. A third film, titled _[The Equalizer 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Equalizer\_3 "The Equalizer 3")_, with Washington and director [Antoine Fuqua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antoine_Fuqua "Antoine Fuqua") returning[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-102)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-103) was released on September 1, 2023.

### 2021 television revival series

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: 2021 television revival series")]

Main article: [The Equalizer (2021 TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(2021_TV_series) "The Equalizer (2021 TV series)")

In November 2019, CBS announced that a reboot was in development with [Queen Latifah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Latifah "Queen Latifah") in the lead role as Robyn McCall. [Andrew Marlowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Marlowe "Andrew Marlowe") and [Terri Miller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terri_Edda_Miller "Terri Edda Miller") were named as showrunners with Latifah herself as an executive producer.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-104) On January 27, 2020, CBS issued a pilot order for the new version.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-105)

The series was among the 14 pilots ordered by CBS in February 2020 and was fast tracked to series the following March, as they are unable to film their pilots where [Universal Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Television "Universal Television") was shut down because of the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-106)

On May 8, 2020, CBS picked up the series[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-107) and they added [Chris Noth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Noth "Chris Noth") as William Bishop, a quirky ex-CIA director who is the opposite of Latifah.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-108) It premiered on February 7, 2021, after [Super Bowl LV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_Bowl_LV "Super Bowl LV").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-109)

### Literature

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Literature")]

Michael Sloan wrote a series of novels about the character. The first is _The Equalizer_, published in 2014, followed by _Killed in Action: An Equalizer Novel_, released in 2018. The novels are a modern reimagining of the original series and focus on McCall leaving The Company and eventually becoming a private investigator in New York. They feature a number of original recurring characters from the television series such as Mickey Kostmayer, Control, and Scott McCall. A third novel, _Equalizer: Requiem_ was released in 2020.

_**The Equalizer**_ is an American [action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film")[crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime "Crime")[drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drama_(film_and_television) "Drama (film and television)") television series, originally airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") from September 18, 1985, to August 24, 1989, which was co-created by [Michael Sloan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Sloan_(television_writer) "Michael Sloan (television writer)") and [Richard Lindheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Lindheim "Richard Lindheim"). It starred the English actor Edward Woodward as Robert McCall, a retired intelligence agent with a mysterious past, who uses the skills from his former career to exact justice on behalf of innocent people who find themselves in dangerous circumstances, while sometimes also dealing with people from his past in covert operations who want to pull him back in or settle old scores. In the years after its cancellation, the show has received a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-CultRant-1) that inspired further works, including [three feature films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#Film_series) and a [re-imagined series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(2021_TV_series) "The Equalizer (2021 TV series)").

## Series plot elements

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Series plot elements")]

The series stars British actor Edward Woodward as Robert McCall, a former [covert operations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Covert_operations "Covert operations") officer of an unnamed American government intelligence organization, which was often referred to simply as "the Agency" or "the Company", who tries to atone for his past by offering, usually free of charge, his services as a troubleshooter, a protector, and an investigator.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer01-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)

People in need found him through a newspaper [classified ad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Classified_ad "Classified ad"): "Got a problem? Odds against you? Call the Equalizer: 212 555 4200."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer04-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5) When he began the business in the pilot episode, the nickname "Equalizer" was revealed as bestowed on him by an operative named "Brahms", played by [Jerry Stiller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Stiller "Jerry Stiller").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3)

Aided by a group of sometimes mysterious contacts, some of whom date back to his spying days, McCall traverses the streets of [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"), delivering justice upon bullies, corrupt police officials and politicians, hoodlums, mobsters, rapists, racists, murderers, kidnappers, drug dealers, and other "truly deserving" people. "Please don't do anything you will never live to regret," he tells one villain.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer06-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-7)

His contacts were also prone to human foibles that ranged from egoism to domestic problems.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5)

Many episodes focused on McCall interacting with "Control" (played by [Robert Lansing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Lansing_(actor) "Robert Lansing (actor)")), the unnamed head of the Manhattan office of the secret organization for which McCall used to work.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer05-3) As a general rule, however, the people responding to the newspaper ad were unremarkable, average, and unknown.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer03-8)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer06-6)

McCall's [Jaguar XJ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaguar_XJ "Jaguar XJ")[saloon car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saloon_car "Saloon car"), weapons, and other gadgetry at times featured significantly as elements in the plot.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Equalizer02-5)

## Cast and characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast and characters")]

### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   Edward Woodward as Robert McCall: A veteran operative of The Company who becomes disillusioned with sacrificing ordinary people for the perceived greater good. He quits and takes out a newspaper advert offering his services to those who need it as The Equalizer. McCall himself is divorced, a "lost dad" long estranged from his son, Scott ([William Zabka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Zabka "William Zabka")). Woodward was nominated for an Emmy for Outstanding Actor in a Drama Series four years in a row but never won, and was also nominated in 1986 and 1987 for the Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Television Series Drama, winning in 1986.
*   [Keith Szarabajka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Szarabajka "Keith Szarabajka") as Michael "Mickey" Kostmayer (Also starring, 56 episodes): a former [Navy SEAL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navy_SEAL "Navy SEAL"), who was thrown in the brig for a crime he did not commit, until McCall cleared him and recommended he join The Company. He is often utilized to surveil suspects and protect clients and witnesses.

## Music

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Music")]

The show's theme music was created by composer/performer [Stewart Copeland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stewart_Copeland "Stewart Copeland"). The track is called "Busy Equalizing". An extended version appears on his album _The Equalizer and Other Cliff Hangers._

Six episodes in the 1988 season were scored by [Joseph Conlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Conlan "Joseph Conlan") and the final season was scored by [Cameron Allan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameron_Allan "Cameron Allan"). Other episodes were scored by [John Cacavas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Cacavas "John Cacavas").

The show ran for four seasons of 22 episodes each. It was initially renewed for a fifth season (causing Keith Szarabajka to turn down a role on _[Midnight Caller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight\_Caller "Midnight Caller")_). In _The Story of The Equalizer_, created for the DVD box set, executive producer Coleman Luck also stated that Universal requested a script for a [crossover episode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossover_episode "Crossover episode") with _[Magnum, P.I.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magnum,\_P.I. "Magnum, P.I.")_ despite the objections of the _Equalizer_ crew as its dark tone was much different than _Magnum_'s much lighter and sunnier style. Ultimately the episode was never filmed, but its script was adapted and changed, airing as the episode "Beyond Control".

### Critical response

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Critical response")]

After the broadcast of the first episode in September 1985, the show received mixed reviews. Critic [Tom Shales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Shales "Tom Shales") wrote in _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ that "to judge from this very attractively atmospheric premiere, [the show] could become a welcome guest in many an American home".[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-87) However, for _[People](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People\_(magazine) "People (magazine)")_, [Jeff Jarvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarvis "Jeff Jarvis") wrote, "The plot’s confusing and the show's as erratic as a [pacemaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacemaker "Pacemaker") on low batteries".[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-88)

## Localizations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Localizations")]

The series was translated into [Afrikaans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Afrikaans "Afrikaans") for broadcast through South Africa's [SABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SABC "SABC") as _Die laaste uitweg_.

The series was broadcast throughout the Arab World with Arabic subtitles during the 1990s, like in Egypt through [Channel 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_in_Egypt "Television in Egypt") and Saudi Arabia through [Saudi 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saudi_2 "Saudi 2").[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-93)

## Home media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Home media")]

On February 12, 2008, [Universal Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Studios_Home_Entertainment "Universal Studios Home Entertainment") released Season 1 of _The Equalizer_ on [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD-Video "DVD-Video") in Region 1 (US only).[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs1-94)

On May 15, 2013, it was announced that [Visual Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Entertainment "Visual Entertainment") had acquired the rights to the series in Region 1.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDplan-95) They subsequently released season 2 on DVD on August 26, 2014.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs3-96)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-SoDVDs2-97) Season 3 was released on October 25, 2014, followed by season 4 on November 24, 2014.

[Visual Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_Entertainment "Visual Entertainment") also released a limited edition complete series set on DVD on August 19, 2014.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-VisualEntertainment.tv-98)_The Equalizer Complete Collection Limited Edition_ set contains all 88 episodes plus 12 hours of bonus content including _[CI5: The New Professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CI5:\_The\_New\_Professionals "CI5: The New Professionals")_; the last film ever done by Edward Woodward, _A Congregation of Ghosts_; and _The Story of The Equalizer_ featuring interviews with cast and crew.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-VisualEntertainment.tv-98)

In Region 2, Universal Playback UK released season 1 on DVD on April 21, 2008. In late 2011, Fabulous Films announced that they had acquired the rights to the series. They have subsequently released seasons 2–4.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-FabFilms-99) On May 27, 2013, Fabulous Films released _The Equalizer: The Complete Collection_ on DVD.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-FabFilmsCC-100) This 24-disc box set contains all 88 episodes of the series as well as bonus content including an all-new documentary featuring interviews with cast and crew.

For the Region 1 DVD's many of the music apart from the theme and scoring by Stewart Copeland has been replaced by cover versions due to the costs for music licensing. In contrast, the Region 2 version contains all of the original music intact.

In Region 4, Umbrella Entertainment has released all four seasons on DVD in Australia.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Equalizer_(1985_TV_series)#cite_note-Umbrel4-101)
